claim: The term record was kept during the term rather than reconstructed after it, and the self-imposed prose-to-code measure was written down with a re-derivable baseline before the work it constrains.
falsified_by: the baseline failing to re-derive at anoieu 579aae7, or docs/history.md turning out to have been written in one sitting near the close of the stretch rather than across it -- both readable from `git log -- docs/history.md` in kanon
scope: two full days of one unfinished term in one repository; says nothing about whether the record is accurate, only that it was kept while it could still be contradicted, and the ratio reading is interim

claim: Prefixes are retired in the tree rather than left to linger: five death candidates against sixty-seven births, three of the five inside the current stretch.
falsified_by: the same paths reappearing under a different prefix in a later run, which would make these moves rather than retirements -- the transplant detector would carry it and did not here
scope: prefix-level only, at prefix_depth 1; a file deleted inside a surviving prefix produces no candidate and this says nothing about those

claim: A hand-written source list three repositories short of the register under-reports the current stretch by 19.9% while under-reporting the whole history by only 4.2%, because the unread trees are the newest ones.
falsified_by: a run of the seven-source subject at this pin reporting a stretch-window total within a few percent of 221 -- which would mean the newest trees are not where the recent work is
scope: the stretch-window half is hand-read and not a pipeline product; the percentages are commit counts only and say nothing about the size or value of the commits

claim: The governance detector is blind to the documents this family governs itself with: seventy-five candidates over twelve source/path pairs across 1,355 commits, none of them laws.md, history.md, board.md, discussion.md, glossary.md or protocols.md.
falsified_by: any governance candidate in this run whose path is one of those six files; or a demonstration that changes to them are reliably accompanied by changes to policy.md or roles.md, which would make the detector's coverage adequate by proxy
scope: a defect in one detector's compiled-in filename list, not a claim that governance changes went unrecorded by the family -- kanon's own documents record them

claim: The register's transition history was truncated by the governance handoff, so seven of ten members produce no joined event and twenty-nine entries appear as listed at inventory start on a single afternoon.
falsified_by: the detector following the register across the repository boundary and emitting joined candidates for logos, eudaimonia, dokimasia, koine, epikrisis and kanon at their recorded join commits, which the register's own `joined` field names
scope: the inventory detector only; the underlying transitions are not lost -- they are in anoieu's history, in a tree this detector does not follow

claim: The tree holding 52.5% of the ecosystem's recorded history contributed no commits to the current stretch, while the tree holding its governance contributed 38% of them.
falsified_by: logos commits landing in the window on inspection of `git log --since` at the pinned commit, or the stretch closing with logos activity that makes this a pause inside the term rather than absence across it
scope: commit counts in an unclosed three-day window, hand-read; a repository can be worked on without commits landing, and this measures landings only

claim: Result data is classified as prose, so the ratio measure reported tachyon at 1,098:1 and a 99% ecosystem-wide prose share in the first run to contain a tree that ships measurement data.
falsified_by: the files under tools/heuresis/ledger/data/ turning out to be hand-written rather than generated, which would make the classification correct and the number real
scope: the extension-based classifier only; the prose-to-code findings elsewhere in this report use a corrected split and are marked as hand-read

claim: Seven repositories stopped within twenty-four hours of each other and resumed within forty-eight, and none of the 169 extracted claims accounts for the twelve-day gap.
falsified_by: a dated claim in any source's declared record naming the period 2026-09-02 to 2026-09-14, which would move all seven candidates out of derived-only
scope: absence from the extracted claims, not absence from the family's documents -- the extractor reads four claim kinds and 80 of the 169 it found are undated

claim: The run machinery writes the run stamp into the pinned date field, which makes panel unrunnable on any labelled run, including six of the twelve already committed to this repository.
falsified_by: panel completing against runs/eunoia-ecosystem/2026-09-02-census, which it does not -- it raises ValueError on the pinned field
scope: a defect in this tool's run bookkeeping; it corrupts no evidence already written and changes no figure in this report

claim: Agent disclosure went to zero across all ten trees for the whole of the stretch, having been non-zero in three of them beforehand, and the pipeline cannot distinguish that from work no agent touched.
falsified_by: an agent trailer on any commit in the window under the detector's own name-field test, in any of the ten trees
scope: disclosure and never contribution; a trailer is opt-in, so the floor is zero and there is no ceiling, and this is not evidence about who or what wrote anything

claim: The delta matcher produced its largest match count to date and every one of the fourteen matches is a word collision on a prefix name, so the count rises with corpus size while the information stays at zero.
falsified_by: any one of the fourteen matched pairs turning out to describe the same event on inspection -- they were read individually and none does; a reader can repeat that from delta.json and claims.jsonl
scope: the matcher only, and this family's habit of naming directories after the things it writes about; a corpus whose prefix names are not common words in its documents would not collide this way
